comparison.explanation: The admission policy rebuilds only the cold objects (one per scan step); the FIFO model rebuilds those plus hot bodies its eviction displaced. The LRU model re-references the whole hot set every scan step, so it too keeps the hot set resident on this interleaved trace; the admission policy matches it while staying a bounded, O(1)-amortised approximate cache.

fifo_model.note: analytic replay of the pre-Phase-49 insertion-ordered FIFO over the identical key trace

lru_model.note: analytic replay of a faithful LRU over the identical key trace

note: Single-run, single-host measurement. The planner's volatile caches hold re-derivable structures (parsed EKBLOOM bodies + their precompiled read plans, region payload bodies, coverage tables); evicting one forgets only a cached parse, never the committed manifestation. This court measures the *observable* effect of the Phase 49 scan-resistant admission policy through the planner's public API: during a one-pass cold scan far larger than the cache, every interleaved hot read is a body-cache hit, so the only body-plan rebuilds are the cold objects themselves. The 'fifo_model' and 'lru_model' figures are analytic replays of two baseline eviction policies (pre-Phase-49 insertion-ordered FIFO, and a faithful LRU) over the identical key trace -- models of the policies, not a second filesystem run -- and 'policy_comparison' states the scan-phase hit rate and rebuild count for all three.
